expected_output.reasoning:
The expected root cause centers on a card-testing burst from 198.51.100.30 (POST /checkout/payment only, ~458 reqs in ~17 seconds at 18:05-18:06) being the primary abusive/malicious pattern, with the Artillery traffic (198.51.100.10) explicitly characterized as known/legitimate automation (not abuse), and a secondary tail of a sensitive-path scan from 198.51.100.20. The recommended fix is a new rate-based rule scoped specifically to POST /checkout/payment.

The investigation instead identifies the Artillery load-test from 198.51.100.10 as the ROOT CAUSE of the incident, treating it as the abusive flood that caused the 5xx spike. It mentions 198.51.100.30 only briefly as 'also over the limit' with generic Chrome UA traffic, without identifying it as a card-testing attack on /checkout/payment specifically, and without recognizing it as the primary malicious actor. The investigation got the roles reversed: it treated the known-automation (Artillery) as the abusive root cause, and failed to recognize the actual card-testing burst from 198.51.100.30 as the key security incident. This is a fundamentally different root cause attribution.
expected_output.evidence: "Root Cause: Artillery load-test from a single IP flooded the origin, undetected-but-not-blocked... A load-generation client (Artillery...) from a single US IP 198.51.100.10 sent 33,609 requests... This is the originating driver" vs expected "(1) A card-testing burst from one client, 198.51.100.30: POST /checkout/payment only... (2) The steady high-volume load-test client 198.51.100.10 (Artillery) also exceeds the rate limit and is only counted; it is known automation, not abuse."
